sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Foreign Market Feasibility Study and Regulatory Licensing Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic tradition; commercial and financial legislation incorporates common-law-inspired concepts, notably the SCSp limited partnership regime of 2016)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) - People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty, signed 4 June 1984, in force 1986
Luxembourg - People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement, signed 16 May 1985, as amended by the Protocol of 2014
EU - China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI), signed 30 December 2020, not yet in force
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49 and 63 (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital within the EU/EEA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016 (instituting Articles 103-1 et seq. creating the Societe en Commandite Speciale regime); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended in particular by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 21 March 2023; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2019 on the operation of the Luxembourg Business Registers.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted: competent Luxembourg authorities, AML/CFT obliged entities conducting customer due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; general public access invalidated by the Court of Justice of the European Union in Case C-37/20, WM and Sovim SA v Luxembourg, 22 November 2022)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents of the corporate General Partner (extrait du registre des societes / certificate of good standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the General Partner's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (effective for China from 7 November 2023) or, for non-Convention states, full consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) granted by the partners in favor of the Luxembourg incorporation agent, notary or registered-office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, together with notarized signature certification if required by the Luxembourg notary or law firm

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports and proof of residential address of each beneficial owner (25% or more) and of the designated manager(s) of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, consular officer, or licensed professional in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the Luxembourg AML/KYC file cannot otherwise be verified through independent sources

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds/source-of-wealth declaration for each beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the partnership interests
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating regulated bank or financial institution holding the client relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consularized copy where the issuing bank's direct confirmation cannot be obtained; otherwise original bank letter accepted under the Luxembourg AML law as a third-party due diligence document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and documented screening of all UBOs (25% or more), the General Partner, designated managers and authorized signatories against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (FISMA/European Commission), (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List and sectoral sanctions determinations, and (iv) Luxembourg domestic vigilance indicators issued by the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers, CRF) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification is mandatory under the amended Law of 12 November 2004; enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for foreign PEPs and their family members and close associates. Negative-news screening must be evidenced in the client file and refreshed immediately prior to closing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), online portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings must be submitted in French or German, the administrative languages of the register; an English-language SCSp partnership agreement must be accompanied by a certified French or German translation. The corporate name must be rendered in Latin script; names originating in non-Latin scripts require a certified transliteration. The name of the partnership must include the suffix 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The selected denomination must comply with the statutory principles of lawfulness (no public-policy violation), truthfulness (no misleading reference to activities or legal form), and exclusivity (no identity with or confusing similarity to any name already appearing in the RCS).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Banking (reserved for credit institutions licensed by the CSSF)
Assurance / Insurance / Reassurance / Reinsurance (reserved for insurers licensed by the CAA)
Fonds / Fund / SICAV / SICAF / RAIF (reserved for CSSF-authorized or notified collective investment undertakings)
Fiducie / Trust / Trustee (reserved for regulated trust companies or expressly authorized professions)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Exchange (reserved for regulated market operators)
Etat / State / National / Municipal / Gouvernement / Ministry (misleading affiliation with the Luxembourg State)
Luxembourg / Letzebuerg (requires prior written authorization of the Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy for use in a commercial name)
Cooperative / Caisse d'Epargne / Savings (reserved for specific licensed legal forms)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A denomination may be reserved online via the LBR portal for 40 days, renewable once for a further 40-day period upon payment of the statutory fee and before expiry of the initial reservation; after expiry without renewal the name is released into the pool. Upon rejection by the RCS/LBR, the formation agent shall: (i) request an internal review or rectification from LBR within 15 days of the refusal notice; (ii) if the ground is confusing similarity, submit a notarized letter of consent from the prior name holder; (iii) if unresolved, lodge a judicial appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (District Court) within the statutory three-month limitation period, acting through Luxembourg-avocat counsel; and (iv) in parallel, file a new distinctive denomination to avoid delay in the incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for a non-regulated SCSp engaged in management consultancy, provided the registered office is a physical Luxembourg street address where legal process can be served and where the partnership's administrative records are kept; the address is typically provided by a duly licensed trust and company service provider (domiciliation agent) regulated under Luxembourg law. A mail-drop-only arrangement with no authorized process-receiving capacity is not accepted by the RCS. No minimum employee headcount, payroll or premises is imposed by company law at formation; however, claiming tax treaty benefits or VAT registration without genuine substance will attract enhanced tax-administration scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: below 5% annualized probability of an unannounced physical inspection for an unregulated, fiscally transparent market-entry consultancy SCSp with no employees and no CSSF authorization. The probability rises to approximately 15% if the SCSp claims corporate income tax treaty benefits, applies for VAT refunds, or files RBE data that is inconsistent with the commercial substance declared; in such cases the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD/AEDT) and social security authorities may conduct desk-based substance checks and, exceptionally, physical verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR/RCS online denomination reservation fee (40-day reservation of the SCSp corporate name)
RCS incorporation registration and RESA publication fee for the Societe en Commandite Speciale (single application including publication in the Recueil electronique des societes et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS fee schedule as published by LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation services for the SCSp for an initial 12-month period (licensed TCSP domiciliation agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg trust and company service provider (domiciliation agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately EUR 100 per month including registered-office certificate and yearly RCS attestation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed for the SCSp formation (authentic act executed by a Luxembourg notary; recommended for overseas KYC acceptance and bank account opening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duche de Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 350-500 all-in for a standard SCSp deed with notarized signature and registry formalities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial RBE (Register of Beneficial Owners) electronic filing of the SCSp beneficial ownership particulars
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre des beneficiaires effectifs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic filing tariff published by LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC compliance pack production: UBO piercing analysis, PEP and OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, negative-news checks, and preparation of the source-of-funds file for all 25%+ beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (cabinet d'avocats) engaged for the formation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 250-350 per hour; fixed fee for a standard non-regulated consultancy SCSp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of overseas corporate documents, power of attorney, and passport/address certifications for the Chinese or other foreign General Partner and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (or local foreign affairs office) of the document's country of origin, plus the Luxembourg Consulate or Embassy where consular legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fees of the issuing authorities and prevailing consular fee schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of the SCSp partnership agreement and supporting documents into French or German for RCS filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified (sworn) translator accredited with the Luxembourg courts or the local authority of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 250-350 depending on document volume

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Article 101 et seq., as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013 on the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); supplemented by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and the Law of 2 September 2011 on the freedom of establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg-Kirchberg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation (RCS registration application) filed together with the executed partnership contract (contrat de société), optionally executed as a notarial deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital: the SCSp capital is freely fixed in the partnership agreement and may be subscribed without immediate payment absent contrary agreement. No escrow or blocked-account requirement applies. Official RCS registration fee tiers by declared capital: EUR 19 (approx. USD 21) below EUR 12,500; EUR 75 from EUR 12,500 to EUR 100,000; EUR 150 above EUR 100,000; RESA publication carries a separate EUR 19 fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Partners, acting as constitutive assembly, adopt the partnership agreement of the Luxembourg Special Limited Partnership (Société en Commandite Spéciale) under Article 101 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013). RESOLVED FURTHER, that [●] be appointed general partner (associé gérant) with sole management authority, and that the registered office be fixed at [●], Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that limited partners subscribe the interests per the contribution schedule, that contributions be paid into the partnership's bank account, and that the general partner be authorized to complete RCS registration, tax registration, bank account opening, and all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - online central register and eJustice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the RCS central database to confirm availability of the proposed corporate name and the mandatory legal-form suffix ('Société en Commandite Spéciale' or 'S.C.Sp.'); reserve the commercial name if required by the domiciliation agent.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name
Identity and nationality of the future general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts, an alternative name can be filed immediately with no re-filing penalty; a named-objection decision may be appealed to the District Court of Luxembourg within 3 months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the partnership agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional) or the partners and their Luxembourg counsel; deed registration with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the SCSp contract either as a private deed (sous seing privé) signed by all partners or as a notarial deed for enhanced evidentiary standing. The contract must identify the general partner, name the limited partners, fix the fiscal year, capital, contribution schedule, profit-sharing rules and transfer regime.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Valid identity documents or passports of all partners
Power of attorney for any signatory acting on behalf of a partner
Registered-office draft agreement or lease/domiciliation consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omission may be cured by a rectificatory deed or an addendum executed by the same partners, which is then filed alongside the original at RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and issuance of the RCS number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), via the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing or a registered Luxembourg agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration application with the executed partnership contract, evidence of the registered office, and identification of the general partner; pay the fee per the declared capital tier; obtain the RCS registration number (numéro d'immatriculation), which evidences legal existence.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS registration form (demande d'immatriculation)
Original or notarized copy of the partnership contract
Consent of the registered-office provider or landlord
Identification documents of the general partner and initial gérant
Proof of payment of RCS fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rectification notice, resubmit the corrected dossier within the stated period (statutory maximum 1 month) to preserve the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic compendium
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, LBR automatically publishes an extract of the filing in RESA; verify the published extract and note the effective date vis-à-vis third parties, particularly for the appointment of the general partner.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract (automatically generated by LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any inaccuracy in the published notice can be corrected by filing a rectification request with LBR, supported by the RCS extract and a copy of the partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax identification, VAT and UBO registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE/LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the national tax identification number through ACD; file the VAT registration application with AEDT if the partnership will supply taxable management-consulting services (including intra-community B2B services, observing the reverse-charge place-of-supply regime); file the beneficial-owner declaration with the RBE register within one month of RCS registration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Executed partnership agreement
ACD affiliation form and AEDT VAT application
UBO declaration form with identification of each beneficial owner
Bank account details for correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax number is not issued within the statutory window, the lodgment of the RCS extract and the executed partnership contract with the ACD single counter triggers an ex-officio assignment; VAT registration may be antedated to the RCS effective date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and social security registration (if staff are engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institutions or authorized e-money institutions (e.g., Wise B2B); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a professional account in the name of the SCSp for capital contributions and operating cash flows; configure the approved payment rails (Wise B2B and bank wire) for client receipts; register the partnership with CCSS and obtain the employer matricule when any employee is hired; maintain the register of partners.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Executed partnership contract
KYC forms and identity documents of partners and UBOs
Proof of registered office address
Projected staffing declaration (for CCSS registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refusal by one bank does not bar formation; the partnership may apply to another institution or evoke the banking mediation procedure of the Luxembourg financial regulator (CSSF) for unreasonable refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal administration of the registered office (Administration communale) for premises notification; the Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) holds no licensing mandate for ISIC 7020 advisory activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable: foreign-market-entry consultancy (ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541611) is not a regulated trade under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the freedom of establishment, and no establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) is required. The operative prerequisites are RCS registration, tax registration and, if applicable, VAT registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: office-based consultancy activities do not fall within the annexes of the Luxembourg Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; neither EIA screening nor an environmental report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission sources exist in a consultancy office environment; applicable obligations are limited to municipal waste segregation, compliance with national waste-register rules if waste thresholds are met, and routing of e-waste (WEEE) to approved recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety is covered by the building owner's conformity certificate for non-public office premises; any premises open to the public require clearance by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS). Structural, electrical and accessibility conformity must be evidenced by the lessor's engineering certificate, and the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) workplace-health rules apply from the first hire.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration - for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax and withholding obligations; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority - for VAT and registration duties; both operating under the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance. Digital access is provided through the MyGuichet.lu national e-government portal and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal (lbr.lu) for RCS filings, statutory filings and legal entity data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Formation/registration: the Luxembourg SCSp or a foreign branch is filed electronically with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) through the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); each registered entity is assigned a unique 13-digit national identification number (matricule / numéro d'immatriculation), which constitutes the primary statutory tax and legal identifier. Step 2 - VAT registration: the RCS-registered entity files a VAT registration application with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu, providing business activity code, place of establishment, anticipated turnover, bank details and expected supplies; a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro d'identification à la TVA) is then issued. Non-established foreign suppliers must register whenever Luxembourg is the place of supply and no reverse charge mechanism applies. Step 3 - Direct-tax file: the ACD opens a partnership direct-tax dossier, and the SCSp files an annual fiscally-transparent partnership declaration; each partner (resident or non-resident) is separately assessed on its allocable share of the SCSp's Luxembourg-source income. Step 4 - Ancillary registrations: customs EORI number for export/import activities, CCSS social security registration if employing Luxembourg staff, and VIES/Intrastat identification for intra-EU supplies where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' classification regime; fiscal transparency of the SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is mandatory under Luxembourg income tax law, which attributes the partnership's profits directly to partners in proportion to their partnership share, regardless of distribution. Therefore, no domestic election is available to convert the SCSp into an opaque corporation. Relevant available mechanisms include: (i) the partnership agreement, which governs profit allocation and is binding for Luxembourg tax purposes subject to anti-abuse and fiscal-substance rules; (ii) voluntary VAT registration and election for the Article 57 small-enterprise VAT exemption via the AEDT; (iii) hybrid-mismatch treatment arising from a foreign jurisdiction's classification of the SCSp as opaque, addressed under the Luxembourg ATAD/ATAD 2 implementing legislation, which may disallow deductions or impose correlative adjustments for cross-border mismatches; (iv) advance pricing arrangements (APAs) and unilateral/bilateral transfer-pricing rulings with the ACD for cross-border consultancy fee structures; and (v) contractual structuring of partner capital accounts to balance Luxembourg taxation versus foreign investor tax positions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-enterprise VAT exemption (Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, as amended for the covered tax year). Non-established foreign suppliers have no general de minimis registration threshold for taxable supplies made in Luxembourg and must register whenever Luxembourg is the place of supply without an applicable reverse charge. EU distance sales of goods to Luxembourg consumers trigger Luxembourg registration above the cross-border distance-selling threshold of EUR 100,000 per calendar year, while non-EU suppliers of B2C electronically supplied services must register in Luxembourg irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no general real-time fiscal clearance regime, no continuous transaction controls, and no mandatory digital stamping/API-based national clearance portal for B2B invoices as of 1 January 2025. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies under the law of 16 May 2019 (transposing EU Directive 2014/55/EU): invoices addressed to Luxembourg public contracting authorities must be structured electronic invoices in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format transmitted via the PEPPOL network. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, but every VAT invoice must satisfy the substantive statutory requirements - complete supplier and customer identification, VAT identification numbers, sequential invoice numbering, date of issue, description, taxable basis, applicable VAT rate, zero-rating/outside-scope reference, and reverse-charge mention where relevant. The EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) proposal will likely introduce standardized transaction-level e-invoicing and reporting by 2030, but no national mandate is in force for the tax period covered by this dossier.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: the 0% export VAT rate applies only where tangible goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier or for its account, an outward customs export declaration is filed, and definitive proof of EU exit is obtained; shipments moving through multiple Member States require a final customs export declaration in the state of exit under the Union Customs Code. Services: cross-border B2B consultancy services of the ISIC 7020 overseas-market-entry type are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (not zero-rated) where the recipient is a non-resident/non-EU business customer, regardless of where the consultant performs the work; such supplies are reported in the 'outside scope' section of the Luxembourg VAT return and are subject to the customer's domestic place-of-supply rules and reverse-charge mechanism. Intra-EU B2B services to business customers holding a valid EU VAT ID are likewise outside Luxembourg VAT through the B2B place-of-supply rule, with VIES recapitulative statements filed where required. Documentary proof of export must be secured within 90 days from dispatch; a supplier failing to hold contemporaneous proof must self-assess Luxembourg VAT at 17% on the exported consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD) with electronic export exit confirmation and goods movement reference
Bill of Lading (sea freight), Airway Bill (air freight), CMR consignment note (road freight) or intermodal transport document evidencing physical exit from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT/MT103 or equivalent) evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds on arm's-length commercial terms
Commercial invoice with detailed quantity, unit value, Incoterms, currency and express indication of the 0% rate or outside-scope treatment
Purchase order or consultancy services contract defining the scope, deliverables, timeline and pricing basis for the ISIC 7020 market-entry consultancy services
Packing list and customs packing declaration where tangible ancillary goods are exported
Luxembourg VAT return reconciliation, export listings, and VIES/Intrastat declarations applicable to intra-EU movements
Customs representation mandate or power of attorney where the SCSp acts through a licensed customs broker
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and the ACD may jointly audit export files, underlying contractual substance, beneficial ownership, bank flows and payment timing. Missing or late export proof triggers: (i) retrospective reversal of the 0% rate or outside-scope treatment; (ii) assessment of Luxembourg VAT at 17% on the full invoiced consideration; (iii) late-payment interest at the statutory rate of 0.6% per month computed from the original due date of the VAT return; (iv) administrative fines and surcharges up to the amount of the tax evaded; and (v) criminal tax-fraud sanctions under the Luxembourg General Tax Law and VAT Law, including imprisonment of generally 8 days to 5 years and fines up to five times the evaded tax where intent is established. The ordinary assessment limitation period is 5 years, extended to a longer limitation window for fraudulent conduct and aggravated cases. Retroactive clawbacks are further reinforced by Luxembourg's general anti-abuse rules, ATAD hybrid-mismatch provisions, and secondary transfer-pricing adjustments, which may recharacterize unrepatriated export receivables as hidden distributions, capital contributions or constructive loans bearing deemed interest. A conservative six-month (180-day) FX repatriation benchmark is therefore maintained for the consultancy's export trade to preserve VAT zero-rating evidence, transfer-pricing consistency and audit credibility.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as a member of the Eurosystem and competent authority for monetary policy, balance of payments statistics, and financial stability oversight in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full eurozone convertibility; Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions under Articles 63-65 TFEU. Profits, capital distributions, and service fees are freely remittable without prior BCL authorisation. The only material obligation is statistical: cross-border transactions above EUR 25,000 must be reported to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes, usually through the executing bank. The SCSp is tax-transparent, so no Luxembourg withholding on distributions arises, and non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg income tax absent a permanent establishment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg has no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or retention-account regime for export proceeds, including proceeds from cross-border consultancy services. Invoices may be collected in EUR or any contract currency, and conversion is executed at free-market rates via commercial banks, subject only to BCL BoP statistical reporting when individual receipts exceed EUR 25,000.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account (EUR) + Capital Escrow (séquestre) sub-account
Operational current account (EUR/USD multi-currency) + Corporate FX and trade desk
Operational current account (EUR/USD) + Cash pooling and segregated agency sub-accounts
Operational current account (EUR) + FX forwards and money-market deposits
Operational current account (EUR) + Correspondent banking services
Wealth-management private account (high minimum balance; unsuitable for a service-oriented SCSp)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium (conditional). Wise Business (Wise Europe SA, an NBB-authorised e-money institution passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2) is viable for small-value multi-currency operating disbursements, such as overseas licence fee wires and contractor payments, and offers superior exchange spreads versus traditional bank wires. It is not suitable as the principal treasury bank: an EMI is not a credit institution, client balances are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit guarantee (FGDL), and the provider cannot offer overdrafts, documentary credits, SWIFT correspondent banking, or FX derivatives. Consequently, the primary corporate and any escrow account must remain with a fully licensed Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not mandate physical on-site attendance for account opening; the CSSF AML/CFT framework permits remote video e-KYC onboarding for standard-risk corporate clients where the bank deploys compliant identification procedures. In current practice, BCEE and BGL BNP Paribas require at least one live video interview of the general partner's authorised signatory and of each UBO holding 25% or more, with corporate documents notarised and apostilled when a partner is domiciled outside the EEA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no legal personality and the ownership chain includes a nominee GP or opaque LP holdings, obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) registration excerpt, fully signed limited partnership agreement (LPA), GP appointment mandates, current RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract, and passports of all individual UBOs holding 25% or more of partnership interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or non-EEA partners from FATF high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned states, or low-tax reputational-risk countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month source-of-funds trail (bank statements, asset disposal deeds, audited financial statements), written source-of-wealth statement, EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening results, and evidence of Luxembourg economic substance (registered office, service contracts, payroll or contractor agreements).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected unlicensed payment-services activity: the entity collects and onward-transfers licence fees on behalf of overseas clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Principal-to-principal consulting agreements showing the SCSp invoices only its own service fee; client regulatory fees either invoiced and paid directly to the overseas regulator or handled under a written agency mandate with a complete audit trail; confirmation that no third-party funds are held overnight except identified service remuneration; any retention of funds structured as a bank séquestre under a triparty escrow agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportion between injected capital, projected fee income, and staffing for a purported market-entry consultancy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with revenue forecasts, concluded consultancy contracts with foreign clients, pipeline evidence, contractor agreements, Luxembourg office lease, VAT registration certificate, and profit-and-loss projections consistent with ISIC 7020 / NAICS 541611 scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection lacking economic rationale or presenting immediate round-tripping or distribution risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution resolution or LPA clause authorising the subscription; full explanation and documentation of the source of the capital contribution; written undertaking to comply with BCL BoP statistical reporting; commitment to deploy funds in identifiable operating expenses rather than immediate distribution to partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital subscriptions from non-resident limited partners arrive via SWIFT MT103 (or Target2 / SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) to the SCSp's BGL BNP Paribas or BCEE account. MT103 Field 70 must reference the BCL Balance-of-Payments purpose category 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital / Partnership Units' together with the subscription reference; the receiving bank verifies the LPA, the RBE extract, and the identity of the remitter before crediting the account. Single transactions exceeding EUR 25,000 are reported to the BCL for BoP statistics, with the execution bank responsible for the filing and the client obliged to supply the purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR payments are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant on the T2 clearing system; non-EUR disbursements (overseas regulator filing fees, foreign contractors, market-entry retainers) use SWIFT MT103 with supporting invoices and the applicable service purpose code through the bank's correspondent network. Documentary collection under URC 522 is occasionally used to link payment against delivery of licences or registration certificates. A Commercial LC (MT700) is not market-standard for consultancy fees, but may support a prepayment obligation when a non-EU regulator or counterparty contractually requires a bank guarantee or standby letter of credit; otherwise direct wire with full documentation is the preferred rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX spot conversion in multi-currency current accounts (non-speculative operating coverage only)
Vanilla FX forward contracts, typically up to 12 months, subject to a bank master agreement (ISDA/EMIR) and available credit line
FX swaps (spot versus forward) for temporary cross-currency liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps permitted only where the SCSp carries a foreign-currency borrowing; full EMIR reporting and clearing obligations apply

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible exclusively for hedging exposures in non-convertible currencies (e.g., CNY/INR) executed through the bank's London or New York desk; speculative FX options or forwards for service companies are not approved under standard Luxembourg credit policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit and publication with Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; FYE 31 December -> filing by 31 July; extension not available for accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts default court fines up to EUR 25,000; persistent non-compliance after formal notice may trigger court-ordered strike-off from RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of Beneficial Owners (UBO) update and validation in the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due on the anniversary of the initial RBE filing; amendments required within 1 month of any change in ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,250; criminal sanctions on repeated or wilful non-disclosure, including imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg partnership income tax return (Form 106 / declaration for tax-transparent partnerships)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing due by 31 May following the taxable year; extended to 31 December for e-filed returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to 10% of assessed partnership tax and penalty tax up to EUR 1,500; fraudulent filing triggers criminal prosecution and summons

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if an SCSp exceeds at least two of the following on a consolidated basis for two consecutive years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce 50 employees. Certain fund SCSp vehicles additionally require audit under CSSF rules when operating as regulated investment fund
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Luxembourg Commercial Code (Plan Comptable Normalisé); IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and mandatory for certain public interest or regulated fund vehicles

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Any transfer of partnership interests in the SCSp must be recorded in the partners register, reflected in the RBE within one month, and followed by an annual RBE confirmation of the recorded data; the SCSp must maintain an up-to-date ownership cascade showing all individuals owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Registre des associés commandés et commanditaires)
Register of Partnership Interests and Transfer Ledger

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined Luxembourg City rate (17% corporate income tax, 6.75% municipal business tax, 7% solidarity surcharge); not imposed on the fiscally transparent SCSp itself, but applied to corporate partners on allocated taxable Luxembourg-source profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Zero entity-level CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax on the SCSp; corporate partners benefit from Luxembourg participation exemption, 80% IP box exemption (effective tax rate approximately 5%), R&D tax credits, and unrestricted CIT loss carry-forward at partner level; the 5-year figure in the schema is retained for municipal business tax modelling consistency

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ACD Model 100 partnership declaration filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu professional portal (Espace professionnel) to the Administration des contributions directes
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 31 December of the calendar year following the SCSp fiscal year-end; an ACD extension may be granted on written request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp identification: name, Luxembourg tax matricule, RCS registration number, registered office, fiscal year start and end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners must be identified in the annex; non-residents are taxable only on Luxembourg PE-attributable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross fee income from overseas market entry consultancy, regulatory licensing work, and foreign feasibility studies
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report only their allocable share of income effectively connected with the Luxembourg business

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business deductions and operating expenses, including subcontractor fees, travel, market research, and licensing agency costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allocated under the partnership agreement; non-resident partners must maintain supporting records in Luxembourg or accessible upon ACD request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result for the fiscal year, before allocation to partners, including capital gains and ordinary business income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp computes income at entity level but passes the net result through to partners according to the partnership agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions disclosure: interest, royalties, management fees, intra-group cost recharges and arm's-length method used
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach transfer pricing documentation and note permanent establishment implications for non-resident related parties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss allocation schedule and carried-forward loss position attributable to each partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may only use Luxembourg tax losses against Luxembourg PE income, not against foreign-source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing demands a fixed ACD penalty up to 10% of the tax due, monthly late payment interest of 0.8%, ex officio assessment, and possible forced dissolution for persistent non-filing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ACD corporate income tax return for corporate partners taxed on SCSp allocations, submitted via MyGuichet.lu professional portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 31 December of the year following the corporate partner's fiscal year-end; extension available through a Luxembourg tax adviser

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base representing the corporate partner's share of SCSp income allocated in accordance with the partnership agreement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners include this amount only to the extent attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption and double tax relief computations, including DTA elimination provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A tax residence certificate (TRC) must be attached if treaty protection is claimed and any Luxembourg source tax was suffered

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss relief and carry-forward computation for the corporate partner alone, not within the transparent SCSp
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit calculations are made at partner level based on the partner's country of residence

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties, late payment interest of 0.8% per month, tax reassessment, and criminal sanctions for intentional concealment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% at SCSp level because distributions by a fiscally transparent partnership are not dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax; the statutory 15% Luxembourg dividend WHT applies only to distributions from resident corporations such as S.A. or S.à r.l.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For any deemed Luxembourg dividend or withheld royalty, the recipient must file a TRC and beneficial ownership declaration with the ACD or the paying agent before payment; Luxembourg DTAs generally reduce dividend WHT to 0%, 5%, 10% or 15%, and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive grants 0% on qualifying EU shareholdings of at least 10% held for 12 months; a refund of excess withholding may be claimed within three years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalty income is 15%, reduced to 0% under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive where a 25% direct shareholding exists; most Luxembourg DTAs reduce royalties to 0-5%; interest carries no Luxembourg withholding tax on ordinary cross-border debt interest

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory local-currency transaction threshold for a Luxembourg Local File; the ACD may require transfer pricing documentation on audit for any related-party transaction, and CbC reporting is mandatory only for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to UAE, but ATAD-based GAAR, abuse of law case law, and ACD tax ruling practice require the SCSp to demonstrate real business substance: local office, employees, directors' decisions, bank accounts and genuine consultancy activity; without commercial substance, treaty benefits may be denied and income reallocated to the true economic owner

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful submission of false SCSp returns, understated consultancy revenues, fictitious expense deductions, or concealment of partner identity from the administration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment plus monthly late interest of 0.8%; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years; forfeiture of tax deductibility
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (associé commandité) is personally and unlimitedly liable for partnership tax debts; managers may face criminal convictions, travel bans, professional disqualification and civil restitution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an SCSp solely to route overseas market-entry fees without employees, premises, business decisions or economic risk while claiming treaty benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of ATAD GAAR; the arrangement may be disregarded, income reattributed to the corporate general partner, and deemed dividend withholding tax of 15% imposed; penalties and interest apply on the revised taxable base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners can be held jointly liable for unpaid taxes resulting from a sham arrangement and may be subject to director disqualification and civil damages

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length management fees, royalty payments or cost recharges to foreign affiliates, or failure to produce Local File documentation when requested by ACD
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustments, 0.8% monthly late interest, documentation penalties, and potential 10% assessment surcharge on under-declared corporate partner income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner's unlimited liability extends to transfer pricing adjustments; deliberate mispricing can trigger criminal fraud liability and personal asset attachment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain the Luxembourg beneficial ownership register, non-identification of ultimate beneficial owners, or accepting third-party payments without AML controls in the consultancy payment chain
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for legal entities under Luxembourg AML law; money laundering exposure carries imprisonment up to five years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance officers and the SCSp general partner face personal criminal liability, fines, and civil restitution for intentional or grossly negligent breaches

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp without RCS registration, without a Luxembourg registered office, or failing to file annual financial statements and tax returns despite commercial activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalties, forced deregistration, ex officio tax assessments, and judicial liquidation procedures initiated by the public prosecutor
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner and effective managers are personally liable for unpaid liabilities after liquidation, and travel restrictions may be imposed for non-observance of Luxembourg court orders
